history.period: Temple built 1989 (per most sources; Justdial lists establishment 1957 - conflict, verify); land purified July 1956 per one source
history.summary: The Mata Lal Devi Mandir at Rani Ka Bagh (Model Town), Amritsar, is dedicated to Mata Lal Devi (1923-1994), a 20th-century female saint of the Marwaha Khatri family, born in Kasoor, Lahore district (now Pakistan). A brahmacharni who lived on milk and fruit, she came to Amritsar after Partition and attained nirvana in 1994. In July 1956 she purified the Model Town plot by observing an 'Ashtami Jagran' on a simple wooden stage; the present temple building dates to 1989 (a Justdial listing gives 1957 - verify which refers to the samstha versus the building). The temple is modelled on the Vaishno Devi shrine at Jammu and is sometimes called a 'mini Vaishno Devi'. Its interior - a maze of mirror-lined corridors, narrow cave-like passages, tunnels, stairs and waterways (the 'Gufa Vaishno Devi Ji') leading to the sanctum - earned it the name Sheesh Mahal. The saint is credited with powers granting children to childless women; women pilgrims form a large part of the devotees. The temple houses idols of many gods and goddesses; photography is not allowed inside. A free bhandara and a charitable hospital serve visitors.

name: Mata Lal Devi Mandir
town_description: Amritsar is Punjab's largest spiritual centre, home to the Golden Temple and a thriving old-city bazaar economy. The Mata Lal Devi Mandir at Rani Ka Bagh/Model Town, about 3.5 km from Harmandir Sahib and 1-2 km from Amritsar Junction (verify), is one of the city's major Hindu pilgrimage sites, visited daily by thousands irrespective of caste or creed.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Dass International Airport - about 12-15 km (verify).
travel.road: 61-62, Rani Ka Bagh, near Model Town, easily accessible from the Grand Trunk Road by auto/taxi (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the 21 February annual birthday celebration is the biggest day.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 5:00 AM-11:00 PM daily (verify - one listing says 4:00 AM-12:00 midnight). Free entry; no photography inside; prasad and free food available.
